_about: P36V.1 Unit B — the ONE shared case table that locks the TypeScript and Python
validation-path formatters to identical behaviour.
The two producers of the Assistant's blocker copy live in different runtimes
(apps/web/src/lib/assistantPaths.ts and apps/api/isaac_api/assistant_paths.py),
so literal code sharing is impossible. This table is the substitute: it is
replayed by BOTH suites — apps/web/src/lib/assistantPaths.test.ts and
apps/api/tests/test_assistant_paths.py — so a change made to one implementation
and not the other fails the other language's tests.
`paths` is the raw locator list as it arrives from the validation response
(exactly what src/isaac_records/official.py emitted, including the literal `$`
root marker, plus the degenerate values a defensive reader must tolerate).
`locations` is the per-locator classification, `technical` is the byte-for-byte
Technical Details payload, and `summary` is the primary user-facing sentence.
A raw `$` may appear in `technical` and MUST NOT appear in `summary`.
`unavailable_cases` locks the SECOND cross-language predicate: telling the API's
validation-CRASH sentinel ({path:'$', message:'Validation could not be
completed.'} — routes.py's defensive except) apart from a genuine root-level
violation. Read through the locator formatter alone the two are identical, and
both producers described the crash as '1 record-level validation issue may be
blocking export' (P36V.1 review IMPORTANT-1).

the sentinel with incidental surrounding whitespace
a GENUINE root-level violation is NOT the sentinel
